config._comment: S1 / S1' boosted-cb tagger. Inputs = the 30 independent MASS-DECORRELATED ak8_gpt_* scores (Sophon-style: a generic massive resonance X, no parent-flavour assumption, so equally valid for H+->cb). S1' adds tau21, tau32, nConstituents. Binary: signal = the 4 gen-matched W->cb jet topologies W(cb)/t2(b'c)/t2(b'b)/t3(b'bc); background = every AK8 jet from the 16 non-Vcb samples. Inputs are written p(..) in the plots so they are never confused with the truth topologies.
config._run_tag_note: output/<run_tag>/ ; dataset_tag selects the input parquet, run_tag names the training run so re-tunes never clobber.
config._train_models_note: S1' dropped as the carried default (agreed: substructure adds ~0 AUC, tau21/tau32/nConstituents rank low) -- also halves wall time on this dataset size (S1 alone took 3412s in the last full run) and reduces exposure to this shared node's memory-pressure kills. Override with train.py --only S1,S1p to train both. M3 added 2026-09-13: the 4-class multiclass sibling of S1 (see M3_* keys below). 2026-09-15, user: S1 REMOVED from train_models -- 'keep only the M3 for the moment (3 classes, each binary)'; the S1 training call is also commented out in 02_train_tagger.py's main(), not just config-gated. The already-trained S1/model.json is untouched and still used by 04_Make_plots.py. Restore 'S1' here (and uncomment the loop in main()) to train it again. n_jobs is no longer hardcoded per-model (was 12) -- 02_train_tagger.py now detects the actual core count via os.sched_getaffinity(0) at runtime and overrides both xgboost.n_jobs and M3_xgboost.n_jobs, since lxplus9 nodes vary in core count.
config._background_keep_prob_note: base build at the top of the 0.2/0.3/0.4/0.5 scan (scan_keep_prob.py); it sub-thins this dataset in-memory so the expensive ROOT read runs once. Final value picked after the scan. 2026-09-15, user: dropped 0.5->0.15 to cut training wall time (topology-0 'true bkg' is 82.6% of train rows at 0.5, tt-semi alone 68.4% of that -- thinning it is the only lever with real leverage on row count; tau21 tightening/loosening were checked and are NOT good levers, see git history). This ONLY affects the thinnable pool (mat topology 0) -- the rare signal-adjacent topologies (Wcb, t2(b'c), proxy, Zbb, QCD(bb)) are NEVER thinned regardless of this value, so their statistics are unaffected. Known tradeoff (already documented in the xgboost regularisation-scan note below): halving the background roughly doubles the residual overtraining bias -- 0.5->0.15 is more than a halving (~3.3x), so re-check the bias numbers after this rebuild+retrain; if bkg bias regresses meaningfully, consider settling between 0.15 and 0.5 rather than pushing lower.
config._class_weight_share_note: the CHOSEN quantity -- target fraction of train-split positive-class sumw per topology: multiplier_c = share_c * total_raw_sumw / raw_sumw_c. Class 6 (Z(bb)-adj) added 2026-09-12: t2_bb's previous 20% share was split into two equal 10% twins -- true t2(b'b) and its Z->bb counterpart -- since z_contamination_study.py showed the tagger cannot distinguish them (mean S1 0.797 for Z(bb)-adj vs 0.834 for true t2(b'b)); every other share is unchanged. Class 7 (QCD(bb)) added 2026-09-13: when it entered the dataset as a topology>0 signal-class member with NO explicit share, it defaulted to raw-weight multiplier 1.0 (the class_weight_lookup fallback), and its very high raw statistics visibly shifted S1's training mix enough to regress overtraining from OK (bkg 3.8%) to FAIL (bkg 15.1%). Giving it a small explicit 2% share re-tames that -- shares now sum to 1.02, not 1.0, which is harmless (the derivation formula does not require the shares to sum to exactly 1; each class's multiplier only depends on its OWN chosen share and raw sumw). Change a share here and just retrain (02_train_tagger.py) -- the multiplier is derived automatically, see class_weight_multiplier below.
config._class_weight_multiplier_note: 2026-09-13: this key is now a REFERENCE SNAPSHOT only (last values derived by 02_train_tagger.py's run on presel_v3_kp50_zbb), not a pipeline input -- 02_train_tagger.py derives it fresh every run from class_weight_share + the real train-split per-class sumw (see derive_class_weight_multiplier() there) and never reads or writes this key, so it can't go stale for the main pipeline. Kept here only because scan_keep_prob.py's standalone class_weight_lookup() still reads this key directly; update it by hand (or fix that script to self-derive too) if you change class_weight_share and want the scan to match. Historical context: unweighted, the 5 signal sub-classes' train-split sumw was Wcb 0.38% / t2_bc 0.16% / t2_bb 0.21% / t3_bbc 0.09% / t2_bc_proxy 99.16% (proxy pulled unthinned from the whole 16-sample background pool, Cabibbo-favoured W->cs vastly outnumbers the dedicated Vcb sample) -- the BDT loss was ~99% 'find a proxy-like jet' and Wcb was noise in the gradient. Applied at LOAD time to TRAIN and VALID weight only -- TEST is left at raw physics weight so reported AUC/working-points/per-class efficiency stay physically meaningful.
config._M3_class_groups_note: 2026-09-13: topology code -> M3 (4-class multiclass: bkg/cb/bb/bbc) class label. cb-like = codes 1,2,5 (Wcb, t2_bc, t2_bc_proxy); bb-like = codes 3,6,7 (t2_bb, Z(bb)-adj, QCD(bb) -- see M3_topo_subshare for the within-class 60/36/4 split; t2_bb/Zbb kept together with QCD(bb) since z_contamination_study.py shows the tagger cannot separate t2_bb/Zbb from the AK8 jet's own inputs alone, and QCD(bb) -- genuine gen-matched QCD-origin bb-bar, see build_trainset.py -- is the same kind of object again; the planned j*-flavour analysis-level cut is a separate follow-on, not part of this model); bbc-like = codes 4,8 (t3_bbc true signal + t3_bcq_proxy_windowed -- 2026-09-18, user: the pre-existing t3bcq_proxy_flag annotation (w_decay==4 & ak8_match_top_bcq, the Cabibbo-favoured b<->light-q swap of t3_bbc) restricted to sqrt(minDR_b^2+minDR_bc^2) in [0.6,1.2] -- see build_trainset.py's BCQ_PROXY_CODE -- and promoted to a real training topology for the first time, same idea as the cb class's t2_bc_proxy); everything else (code 0) = background.
config._M3_class_weight_share_note: 2026-09-13: like class_weight_share, but keyed by the M3 class label (0..3, matching M3_class_names) INCLUDING background -- multi:softprob has no scale_pos_weight equivalent, so background/signal balance must be baked into sample_weight here directly (see derive_multiclass_weight_multiplier() in 02_train_tagger.py), unlike the binary path where scale_pos_weight handles it automatically. Default derived from class_weight_share's existing cb:bb:bbc ratio (which summed to 1.0 over signal only: cb pool codes 1+2+5 = 0.5+0.1+0.1 = 0.7, bb pool codes 3+6 = 0.1+0.1 = 0.2, bbc code 4 = 0.1) rescaled into a 50% combined-signal budget (0.7*0.5=0.35, 0.2*0.5=0.10, 0.1*0.5=0.05) plus an explicit 50% background share chosen to roughly match the effective signal:background balance S1's scale_pos_weight already gives it -- a first-pass choice, not yet tuned; revisit once M3's overtraining/AUC numbers exist.
config._M3_topo_subshare_note: 2026-09-13, user: within the 'bb' class (label 2)'s own 10% overall share, split 60% t2(b'b) / 36% Z(bb)-adj / 4% QCD(bb) -- t2(b'b) prioritised as requested, QCD(bb) capped low because its gen-matched population is tiny (2026-09-13 investigation: ~1.5% of QCD-sample AK8 jets have >=2 hadron-flavour-b AK4 jets in-cone) so 'accept all these events' rather than force a larger share onto a handful of jets. Within the 'cb' class (label 1): FIRST attempt (2026-09-13) used the aggressive 2:1 Wcb-vs-whole-t2(b'c)-family split (Wcb=0.6667, t2_bc=0.0009 natural, proxy=0.3324 natural). 2026-09-14 UPDATE (user, after seeing this push M3 into WARN across the board): moved to an explicit 60/20/20 (Wcb/t2_bc/proxy). Investigated first: cb's own WARN was shown to be driven by the bkg(rest) side (5.1-5.6%), NOT the sig side (0.7%, healthy at either split) -- so this subshare change does not target cb's actual overtraining driver, but is kept as the user's explicit physics-priority choice. Side effect to watch: topo2 (true t2_bc, only 18.9k/4.0k raw train/test events) needs its multiplier raised from ~4.3 (at 0.09% target) to ~960 (at 20% target, ~220x) since its raw sumw is tiny (~0.16% of the cb pool) -- this concentrates much more gradient weight onto a small event population, a similar order of magnitude to bbc's already stats-limited topo4 (10.4k/2.1k), so a new topo2-specific overfitting contribution is plausible and expected, not a bug if seen. Classes not listed here (bbc) are unaffected -- they fall back to natural raw-sumw proportions within the class, i.e. today's single-multiplier-per-class behaviour. 2026-09-17 UPDATE (user): after an 8-point cb-subshare scan (60/20/20, 70/25/5, 80/15/5, 65/18/17, 70/15/15, 75/13/12, 80/10/10, 85/8/7 -- Wcb AUC/Z improves monotonically with Wcb-share, at a monotonic cost to AUC(cb,full) and, past ~80%, to overtraining bias too: 85/8/7 was worst on both cb,full AUC (0.876) and bias despite topping Wcb AUC/Z), moved to 66/17/17 (Wcb/t2_bc/proxy) -- close to the scan's 65/18/17 point (AUC(Wcb) 0.893, Z 0.147, bias 0.6%/0.6%; AUC(cb,full) 0.889, bias 0.6%/2.2%, OK), chosen over the scan's best-AUC/Z point (85/8/7) specifically to avoid that bias/cb-full-AUC degradation. 2026-09-17 UPDATE (user), bb-subshare: moved from 60/36/4 (t2_bb/Zbb/QCDbb) to 66/17/17, ahead of an in-progress 5-point scan (66/17/17, 66/34/0, 66/0/34, 80/10/10, 80/15/5). Partial results at decision time: 60/36/4 AUC(bb,full) 0.940 bias 0.3%/0.7%; 66/17/17 AUC(bb,full) 0.943 bias 1.0%/1.4%; 66/34/0 AUC(bb,full) 0.937 bias 0.3%/0.0%; 66/0/34 AUC(bb,full) 0.945 bias 1.0%/1.1% -- unlike cb, this axis is NOT monotonic (QCD(bb) share trades AUC against bias non-monotonically); 66/17/17 chosen as a balanced point ahead of the scan finishing, not necessarily the AUC-optimal one (66/0/34 was marginally higher on AUC(bb,full) among points completed so far; 80/10/10 and 80/15/5 were still pending at decision time). 2026-09-18 FINAL UPDATE (user, scan complete): cb-subshare set to 80/15/5 (Wcb/t2_bc/proxy; scan: AUC(Wcb) 0.898, Z 0.157, bias 1.1%/1.4%; AUC(cb,full) 0.880, bias 1.0%/2.7%, OK). bb-subshare set to 90/5/5 (t2_bb/Zbb/QCDbb) -- more aggressive than any scanned point (60/36/4 through 80/15/5), not itself scanned; a step further along the same direction the 5-point scan explored. bbc-subshare (NEW, class label 3 previously unlisted/natural-proportion): 95/5 (t3_bbc/t3_bcq_proxy_windowed) -- see M3_class_groups note for what the new code 8 is. 2026-09-18 LATER SAME DAY UPDATE (user, after the 80/15/5-90/5/5-95/5 training's score_M3_* diagnostics -- see chat: h_tot/proxy near-degeneracy investigation): moved AWAY from the more extreme splits toward more balanced ones: cb-subshare 70/15/15 (Wcb/t2_bc/proxy, was 80/15/5 -- less Wcb-dominant, more proxy weight). bb-subshare 80/10/10 (t2_bb/Zbb/QCDbb, was 90/5/5). bbc-subshare 80/20 (t3_bbc/t3_bcq_proxy_windowed, was 95/5, biggest relative jump given it's only 2 components). Prior published diagnostics (score_M3_*.png, panel_M3.png etc, all from the 80/15/5-90/5/5-95/5 run) preserved under the '_prev1' suffix for before/after comparison -- see the gallery/publish-prefix code for the naming.
config._features_S1_note: 22 nodes (2026-09-13: +ak8_gpt_qcd, was 21) = the 30-node ak8_gpt_* set (all minus the 2 REMAINING parent sums topbw/topw) with the 10 leptonic top/W-decay categories merged into one ak8_gpt_lepq = their sum, PLUS the QCD parent sum ak8_gpt_qcd re-added on top of its own 5 children (qcdb/qcdbb/qcdc/qcdcc/qcdothers), on the hypothesis (user, 2026-09-13) that the parent softmax output is not a pure arithmetic sum of the 5 children (unlike the verified-lossless lepq merge) and may carry its own separation power from the model's learned QCD-flavour-composition weighting. If it turns out to be an exact linear combination of the 5 children already in the list, a tree model gains nothing from it (permutation importance should then read ~0) -- next training's permutation-importance ranking is the direct test. topbw/topw stay excluded (not requested). The 10 leptonic top/W-decay categories are mutually-exclusive sub-classes of one GloParT parent softmax, so THEIR sum (lepq) is a verified lossless union probability, not a dropped feature -- and all 10 individually contributed <0.0012 permutation AUC (9 of 10 below 0.001; physically expected since our AK8 jet is a hadronic W->cb candidate). cc/qcdbb/qcdcc/topbwcs/qq/ss/tauhtauh were also individually <0.001 but are NOT merged: they are physically distinct categories (not mutually-exclusive sub-classes of one summed parent), so low permutation importance there means 'not needed for this S:B split', not 'redundant' -- kept as-is per instruction.
config._derived_features_note: computed at LOAD time in train.py/scan_keep_prob.py (df[name] = df[components].sum(axis=1)) -- the raw components stay in the parquet (build_trainset.py always writes them) so this is a train-time-only reduction, reversible with no rebuild. topbwtaumv (auc_drop 0.00113, the highest of the 10) is included for physical consistency of the group; flag if you want it split out separately instead.
config._xgboost_note: point D3 of the regularisation scans: depth 2, min_child_weight 300, subsample 0.5. Background training bias 6.1% (from 14.2%), converges at ~620 of 4000 trees so early stopping decides, 45 s/model. reg_alpha HURTS (10.6%) and max_delta_step does not help. Regularisation saturates ~6%: the residual bias is statistics-limited (halving the background doubles it), so <5% needs background_keep_prob 0.15 -> ~0.40 and a dataset rebuild.
config._M3_xgboost_note: 2026-09-13: SEPARATE, MORE REGULARISED than S1's xgboost block (reused unchanged for S1) -- first-run M3 (identical params to S1) FAILED overtraining on all 3 classes (bias: cb bkg 21.9%, bb sig 13.6%/bkg 15.4%, bbc bkg 144.4%). bbc's own raw test-split stats are tiny (2132 raw events, sumw 3.98) after a target share (5%) that upweights it heavily -- that number is dominated by statistics, not pure overfitting, and won't fully resolve without more raw bbc events (there aren't any more in this MC). cb's asymmetric bias (sig 0.1% / bkg 21.9%) with bkg's own huge stats (1.03M test) pointed at genuine overfitting coupled THROUGH the shared softmax (bbc's severe overfit perturbs every class's logit, since softmax normalises across all 4 at once) rather than a background-specific stats problem -- hence stronger GLOBAL regularisation (higher min_child_weight/reg_lambda, lower subsample/colsample, earlier stopping) as the lever, not a per-class knob (multiclass has no per-class regularisation). Retune this block if bias is still unacceptable after a run; do not just copy S1's numbers back. 2026-09-14: n_estimators 4000->6000 -- the previous full run's validation mlogloss was STILL (very slightly) improving at the 4000-round cap, i.e. early_stopping_rounds=30 never fired, so training was capped rather than converged; letting it run to a genuine early stop costs little (the tail improvement was tiny, ~1.4e-4 over the last 100 rounds) but removes the artificial cap as a confound when reading the next run's bias numbers. 2026-09-15, user: chose between 25/30/35/40 -- replayed the ACTUAL last run's training_history.json (real M3 fit, not a toy) through each patience value: esr=30 is exactly what happened (stopped at round 4196, best at 4166). esr=25 would have stopped 673 rounds earlier (round 3523, best_i=3498) at val_mlogloss 0.55392 vs the true best 0.55276 -- a 0.21% relative cost for ~1225s (~20 min) saved. esr=35/40 give ZERO extra rounds beyond 30 (the real run's last 10 recorded values are flat within 2e-5, so there's nothing more to find past round ~4170 anyway). 25 is the clear pick: real, measurable time savings for a negligible, explicitly-quantified accuracy cost; 35/40 have no evidence of any benefit at all. n_jobs is no longer read from here at runtime -- 02_train_tagger.py overrides it via os.sched_getaffinity(0) (kept as 12 here only as a fallback default for standalone scripts that read this file directly, e.g. scan_keep_prob.py).
